commands.command: dry-run raw and --bounded modes (default, no mutation)
RUN 1: real bounded pause/unpause cycle on typedb -- detected DEGRADED, recovered to READY within the bounded window
RUN 2: real bounded disconnect/reconnect cycle on fuseki, using the corrected HTTP round-trip oracle -- detected unreachable, recovered to reachable within the bounded window
RUN 3: real bounded restart cycle on keycloak -- self-recovers, confirmed healthy within the bounded window

RUN 4 (negative): --bounded rejects reconnect and unpause as primary faults (they are recovery-only halves), and rejects disconnect for spire-server (no published health endpoint to verify from the host)

real, live-verified technical finding: a bare TCP connect (socket.create_connection) to a disconnected service's published port SUCCEEDS on this Docker Desktop host (its port-forwarding proxy completes the handshake independently of container network reachability), while a real HTTP GET correctly fails -- this is why the bounded disconnect oracle is HTTP-based, not port-connect-based

bundled fix discovered while restoring stack state for this evidence capture: deploy/bootstrap/fixtures/load_fixtures.py's TerminusDB not-found check only tolerated the 'HTTP 200 with a Status: 404 text prefix' quirk documented in OCOR-DEV-0081, not a real HTTP 404 for the identical condition, which TerminusDB was also observed to return for the same query across different invocations; fixed to accept both, extended reports/tests/ocor-runtime/tests/tasks/test_ocor_dev_0081.py with a dedicated regression test
pytest ocor-runtime/tests/tasks/test_ocor_dev_0083.py -v (12 unit/negative/contract tests, all subprocess/HTTP calls faked)
full local pytest regression (ocor-runtime/tests/ + 3 reports/tests suites)

requirement_results.command: unit/negative tests for the bounded pause/disconnect/restart cycles and the http_reachable oracle, no live dependency
real bounded pause/unpause cycle on typedb against the live stack
real bounded disconnect/reconnect cycle on fuseki against the live stack, using the corrected HTTP oracle
real bounded restart cycle on keycloak against the live stack
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline

residual_risks: A bounded disconnect cycle is unsupported for SPIRE server/agent (no published host port to probe); pause and restart remain available for them.

The bare-TCP-vs-HTTP-round-trip finding is specific to this host's Docker Desktop networking implementation; a native Linux Docker host's iptables-based port publishing may behave differently, but the HTTP-based oracle is correct and portable either way (a real HTTP round trip is a strictly stronger reachability proof than a bare TCP connect on any platform).

Fixing deploy/bootstrap/fixtures/load_fixtures.py's TerminusDB not-found detection (bundled here, discovered while restoring stack state) changes OCOR-DEV-0081's deliverable after its own acceptance; this is a correctness fix for a real, reproduced defect (TerminusDB returning two different not-found response shapes for the identical condition across invocations), not a scope change, and is covered by a new regression test in that task's own test file.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior WS-12 evidence (no psycopg installed) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every bounded cycle IS a rollback drill by construction: RUN 1-3 each apply a real fault and prove automatic recovery within a bounded window, with a fail-safe finally-block recovery attempt even on detection failure (verified directly by the unit tests, which assert the recovery command runs even when the fault is never detected or the fault command itself fails).
